meta.generated: synthetic demo data, illustrative only — example project: Bellcrest Health System EHR rollout

roles.summary: Bedside nursing on the medical-surgical and telemetry floors across all three hospitals. Charting, vitals, medication pass and care-plan documentation move from a mix of paper flowsheets and a legacy nursing module into the new EHR's structured clinical documentation and eMAR.
before: Vitals and I&O charted on paper flowsheet, transcribed into legacy system at shift end
Medication pass verified against a printed MAR
Care plan updated narratively in free-text nursing notes
Physician verbal orders relayed by phone or in person and transcribed by the unit clerk
after: Vitals entered directly at the bedside via workstation-on-wheels, flows straight into the structured record
Medication pass scanned against the electronic MAR with barcode patient/med matching
Care plan built from structured, problem-based templates with required fields
Physician orders arrive electronically through CPOE with a nursing task queue
constraints: Documentation must be completed at the bedside without disrupting direct patient care
Three-shift rotation means training and go-live support must cover nights and weekends

roles.summary: ED nursing across all three sites, where triage, rapid reassessment and medication administration happen under time pressure. The new EHR replaces a separate ED tracking board and a paper triage form with one structured record shared with the rest of the hospital.
before: Triage acuity recorded on a paper form, re-keyed into the ED tracking board
Medication administration charted after the fact, during a lull
Handoff between shifts relies on a verbal report plus a whiteboard
Discharge instructions printed from a separate template library
after: Triage acuity entered once, drives the electronic tracking board directly
Medications scanned and charted at the point of administration
Structured shift handoff note auto-populates from the record
Discharge instructions generated from the visit record and reconciled medication list
constraints: No workflow change may add a step between triage and first clinical contact
High turnover and agency staff mean training has to work for people who joined after go-live too

roles.summary: Inpatient attending physicians who write the majority of admission, medication and discharge orders. CPOE replaces verbal and handwritten orders with structured order sets and clinical decision support, which is the sharpest authority change in the rollout.
before: Orders written by hand on the chart or given verbally to the unit clerk
Medication choice and dosing left to individual judgement and memory
Drug interaction and allergy checks performed manually or not at all
Discharge orders written the morning of discharge with no structured checklist
after: Orders entered directly into CPOE from structured, evidence-based order sets
Dosing pre-populated with weight-based and renal-adjusted defaults, overridable with a reason
Interaction, allergy and duplicate-therapy alerts fire at order entry, before the order is signed
Discharge order set triggers medication reconciliation and follow-up scheduling automatically
constraints: Order sets must be built and validated by service line before go-live, not improvised on the floor
Physicians split time across all three hospitals, so downtime and training windows can't be site-specific

roles.summary: Coordinates the inpatient unit desk: admits, transfers, discharges and transcribing verbal orders into the chart. CPOE removes the order-transcription task entirely and shifts the role toward exception handling and bed coordination.
before: Transcribes verbal and handwritten physician orders into the chart and notifies the right department
Manages the admission/transfer/discharge paper log
Answers unit phone and relays messages between physicians, nurses and families
Tracks bed status on a whiteboard
after: Orders route electronically to the right department with no transcription step
ADT events tracked directly in the EHR's bed-management module
Message routing partly absorbed by in-system secure messaging
Bed status visible system-wide in real time
constraints: Some unit clerks are the only non-clinical staff on the floor overnight and need a fallback for system downtime
Role is being partly redefined, not eliminated — messaging on this needs to be explicit

roles.summary: Verifies every inpatient medication order before it reaches the floor. CPOE and eMAR route orders directly to pharmacy with automated interaction and duplicate-therapy checking, changing verification from a first pass to an oversight and exception role.
before: Re-keys handwritten or verbal orders into the pharmacy dispensing system before verifying them
Manually checks interactions, allergies and duplicate therapy against reference material
Verification queue managed by paper printout and phone calls to the floor
Dispensing decisions documented informally in a shared log
after: Orders arrive in the verification queue directly from CPOE, no re-keying
System-flagged interaction, allergy and duplicate-therapy alerts surface at verification, pharmacist clears or escalates
Verification queue and turnaround time visible and reportable in the EHR
Every override is captured with a reason code, feeding the medication-safety committee
constraints: Verification turnaround time cannot regress during the transition — it is a patient-safety metric
Alert volume must be tuned pre-go-live or override fatigue defeats the safety benefit

roles.summary: Fills and delivers inpatient medication orders once the pharmacist has verified them. The new system changes the queue technicians work from and adds barcode-driven fill checking, without changing who is allowed to verify or override an order.
before: Fills orders from a printed pick list generated after pharmacist verification
Cross-checks fills manually against the original order
Restocks unit-based automated dispensing cabinets on a fixed round
Logs discrepancies on paper for the pharmacist to review
after: Fills orders from an electronic queue that updates the moment a pharmacist verifies
Barcode scan confirms the correct medication and strength at fill
Cabinet restocking list generated from real-time usage data
Discrepancies logged directly in the system and routed automatically
constraints: Fill accuracy cannot dip during the changeover — this role has no independent verification authority to catch its own errors
Cabinet hardware integration with the new EHR needs to be tested per site before go-live

roles.summary: Rooms patients, takes vitals and documents intake in the outpatient clinics attached to each hospital. Intake moves from a paper rooming sheet into structured EHR templates that feed the physician's note directly.
before: Vitals and chief complaint recorded on a paper rooming sheet
Sheet handed to the physician or scanned into the record later
Medication and allergy list confirmed verbally, updated inconsistently
Intake forms filed separately from the visit note
after: Vitals and chief complaint entered directly into the structured intake template
Intake flows straight into the physician's visit note, no handoff or scanning
Medication and allergy reconciliation is a required, structured step
Intake and visit note live in the same record automatically
constraints: Rooming time budget per patient cannot increase — clinic schedules are already full
Several clinics share float staff across sites, so training has to be site-agnostic

roles.summary: Front-desk registration and appointment scheduling for the outpatient clinics. The clinical EHR module changes downstream documentation more than it changes front-desk work, but the front desk absorbs new patient questions about online check-in and portal access.
before: Registers patients and verifies insurance at the desk
Books and reschedules appointments in the legacy scheduling system
Collects paper intake and consent forms
Answers questions about upcoming visits by phone
after: Registration and insurance verification happen in the same system used clinically
Scheduling shares a calendar with the new patient portal, so online self-scheduling appears on the same screen
Consent forms captured electronically at check-in
Fields many new questions about portal access and online check-in that did not exist before
constraints: Front desks are chronically short-staffed, so any new task has to replace one, not add to the pile
High turnover means the anchor material has to work for someone hired the week after go-live

roles.summary: Central billing office that codes and submits claims from the clinical record. Charge capture now originates from structured EHR documentation instead of a mix of paper superbills and free-text notes, a moderate but back-office-only change.
before: Codes charges from a mix of paper superbills and dictated notes
Chases missing documentation by phone or email
Manually cross-checks charges against the visit schedule
Submits claims through a separate billing system
after: Codes directly from structured EHR documentation with charge-capture prompts built in
Missing-documentation queries route to the ordering provider inside the record
Charges reconcile against the visit schedule automatically
Claims submission integrates with the EHR's billing module
constraints: Claims turnaround cannot slip during go-live month or cash flow is affected
Coding staff need the new charge-capture logic validated against payer rules before go-live, not after

roles.summary: Processes specimens and results for orders placed through CPOE. Orders and results now flow electronically end to end, replacing a paper requisition and a separate results-entry step.
before: Receives paper requisitions alongside physical specimens
Manually matches specimen labels to the requisition
Enters results into a separate lab information system
Calls critical results to the floor and logs the call on paper
after: Receives electronic orders that print a barcode label matched to the specimen
Barcode scan confirms specimen-to-order match automatically
Results flow directly into the EHR from the lab system interface
Critical-result calls are logged in the EHR with an acknowledgement timestamp
constraints: Interface between the lab system and the new EHR must be validated per analyzer before go-live
Turnaround-time targets for critical results are a regulatory requirement and cannot regress

roles.summary: A net-new role created to support the EHR rollout: builds order sets and documentation templates, monitors alert-override rates, and is the first line of triage between clinical staff and IT once the system is live.
before: Role does not exist prior to the EHR rollout
after: Builds and maintains CPOE order sets and documentation templates with clinical input
Monitors clinical decision support override rates and flags alerts that need retuning
Runs the first-line triage queue between floor staff and the IT help desk
Trains super-users on template and order-set changes as they roll out
constraints: Needs a clinical background to be credible with physicians and nurses, which narrows the hiring pool
First cohort has to be trained ahead of every other role, since they help train everyone else

roles.summary: Runs daily staffing and patient assignment on the inpatient units. A new acuity-based staffing module recommends assignments directly from the EHR's patient data, changing a decision the charge nurse used to make unaided.
before: Builds the shift assignment by hand using a whiteboard and personal knowledge of patient acuity
Tracks staffing ratios manually against unit policy
Escalates staffing gaps by phone to the house supervisor
Documents assignment changes on paper for the next shift
after: Reviews a system-generated assignment recommendation based on real-time acuity scores
Staffing ratios calculated and flagged automatically against policy
Escalation queue for staffing gaps runs inside the EHR, visible to the house supervisor in real time
Assignment history is part of the permanent record, not a handwritten handoff
constraints: The recommendation engine has to be tunable per unit — a medical floor and an ICU do not staff the same way
Charge nurses need explicit authority to override the recommendation, or the tool will be worked around
